intro: A pilgrim city of cathedral bells, medieval streets and a lively student scene in the heart of Kent.
areas: Mercery Lane, the Buttermarket and Christ Church Gate.
The medieval gate, Westgate Gardens and river punts.
Independent shops on Palace Street and Northgate.
sights: Mother church of the Anglican Communion, part of a World Heritage Site.
Abbey ruins, also part of the World Heritage Site.
Short punt trips through the old city.
eat: Food market and restaurant by Canterbury West station.
night: Clubs and bars in term time.
arrive: Canterbury West has high-speed trains to London St Pancras (under an hour); Canterbury East serves London Victoria. Gatwick and Heathrow are the nearest major airports.
around: The walled centre is compact and walkable; Stagecoach buses serve the coast and villages.
pass: Stagecoach day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn; December for the Christmas market.
tip: Buy a cathedral ticket in advance on busy summer days.

intro: Kent’s county town on the River Medway, close to Leeds Castle and the orchards of the Garden of England.
areas: Week Street, Fremlin Walk and the High Street.
Medway walks past the Archbishop’s Palace.
sights: Moated castle and gardens a short drive east.
night: Concerts and festivals in Mote Park.
arrive: Maidstone East and Maidstone West stations have trains to London. Gatwick is about 50 minutes by road.
around: Arriva buses serve the town; the centre is walkable.
pass: Arriva day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for castles and gardens.
tip: Visit Leeds Castle early in the day before tour groups arrive.

intro: An elegant spa town with the colonnaded Pantiles, independent shops and the High Weald countryside around it.
areas: Georgian colonnade with the chalybeate spring.
sights: Historic promenade and the spring that founded the town.
arrive: Tunbridge Wells station has trains to London Charing Cross and Cannon Street. Gatwick is about 45 minutes by road.
around: Walkable centre; Arriva and other buses cover the area.
pass: Bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for gardens and outdoor dining.
tip: Taste the spring water at the Pantiles chalybeate spring when a dipper is on duty.

intro: Surrey’s historic county town on the River Wey, with a cobbled High Street, a castle and the North Downs on its doorstep.
areas: Cobbled shopping street with the Guildhall clock.
Walks along the River Wey Navigation.
sights: Norman keep with views over the town.
Riverside walks and boat hire (National Trust).
Walks on the North Downs and St Martha’s Hill.
night: North Street and the High Street.
arrive: Guildford station has trains to London Waterloo (about 35–40 minutes). Heathrow and Gatwick are each about 40 minutes by road.
around: Walkable centre; Stagecoach and Arriva buses.
pass: Bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for the Surrey Hills.
tip: Climb the castle keep for a view across the town.

intro: A relaxed Sussex seaside town with an Art Deco pier, a long promenade and the South Downs behind it.
areas: Promenade, beach huts and Worthing Pier.
sights: Award-winning pier with an Art Deco pavilion.
Iron Age hillfort in the South Downs.
eat: Kiosks and restaurants on the prom.
night: Shows at the head of the pier.
arrive: Worthing station has trains to London Victoria and Brighton. Gatwick is about 40 minutes away.
around: Stagecoach and Brighton & Hove buses run along the coast.
pass: Bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: May–September for the beach.
tip: Hike up to Cissbury Ring for views across the coast.

intro: Golden sands, clifftop gardens and a lively night scene on the Dorset coast.
areas: Lower Gardens, the pier and Bournemouth Beach.
Pier, surf culture and the Chine.
sights: Miles of sand with lifeguards in summer.
Old Harry Rocks and Durdle Door are a short trip away.
night: A big student and party scene.
arrive: Bournemouth Airport has a bus to the town. Bournemouth station has trains to London Waterloo.
around: Morebus and other buses run along the coast; the seafront is great for walking and cycling.
pass: Morebus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: June–September; Bournemouth Air Festival in late summer.
tip: Take the land train or walk the promenade between Bournemouth and Boscombe piers.

intro: A medieval cathedral city with Britain’s tallest spire, the Magna Carta and Stonehenge nearby.
areas: Iron Age hillfort and site of the first cathedral.
sights: Britain’s tallest spire and the best-preserved 1215 Magna Carta.
World Heritage stone circle, about 10 miles north.
eat: Market days on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
The Haunch of Venison and others.
night: Gigs and comedy in a former church.
arrive: Salisbury station has trains to London Waterloo, Bristol and Southampton. Southampton Airport is about 40 minutes away.
around: Walkable centre; Salisbury Reds buses and Stonehenge tour buses.
pass: Bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn; summer and winter solstices at Stonehenge.
tip: Book Stonehenge tickets in advance for a timed entry.

intro: A World Heritage city of honey-coloured Georgian crescents, Roman baths and natural thermal springs.
areas: Abbey, Roman Baths and Pulteney Bridge.
Independent shops and cafés, the ‘artisan quarter’.
sights: Bathe in natural thermal water on a rooftop pool.
Sweeping Georgian terrace; No. 1 is a museum.
Gothic abbey in the city centre.
eat: Historic home of the Bath bun.
night: Cosy inns in the Georgian lanes.
arrive: Bath Spa station has trains to London Paddington and Bristol. Bristol Airport is about an hour away by bus.
around: Walk; the centre is compact but hilly. Buses and Park & Ride for the outskirts.
pass: First and Park & Ride day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn; the Christmas market in late November and December.
tip: Book Thermae Bath Spa at quieter times and visit the Roman Baths early.

intro: Devon’s historic capital, with a Gothic cathedral, Roman walls, a lively quayside and two coasts nearby.
areas: Historic quay with cafés, kayak hire and cycle routes.
sights: Gothic cathedral with the world’s longest unbroken medieval vaulted ceiling.
Historic quayside and the Exe estuary trail.
eat: Devon style: cream first, then jam.
night: Arts centre with gigs and film.
arrive: Exeter Airport has a bus to the city. Exeter St Davids has trains to London Paddington and Waterloo.
around: Walkable centre; Stagecoach buses cover the city and Devon.
pass: Stagecoach day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for Dartmoor and the coast.
tip: Book the Underground Passages tour in advance at busy times.

intro: Britain’s Ocean City, where the Mayflower set sail, with a historic Barbican and wide views from the Hoe.
areas: Historic harbour with cobbled streets, galleries and bars.
Seafront promenade, Smeaton’s Tower and Tinside Lido.
eat: Fresh catch from Plymouth’s fish market.
The oldest working gin distillery in England.
arrive: Plymouth station has trains to London Paddington, Bristol and Cornwall. Exeter Airport is about an hour away. Ferries sail to France and Spain.
around: Citybus and Stagecoach buses; the Hoe and Barbican are walkable.
pass: Citybus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: May–September for the lido and waterfront events.
tip: Take the water taxi from the Barbican to Royal William Yard.

intro: A Regency spa town of elegant terraces, festivals and horse racing on the edge of the Cotswolds.
areas: Pittville Park and the Pump Room.
sights: Home of the Cheltenham Festival every March.
Regency spa building in Pittville Park.
Villages and hills on the doorstep.
night: Jazz, Science, Music and Literature festivals.
arrive: Cheltenham Spa station has trains to Birmingham, Bristol and London. Bristol and Birmingham airports are about an hour away.
around: Walkable centre; Stagecoach buses.
pass: Stagecoach day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: March for racing (book far ahead); May–October for festivals.
tip: During Festival week in March, hotels across the county sell out months ahead.

intro: A riverside cathedral city known for porcelain, Worcestershire sauce and cricket on the Severn.
areas: The Severn, the racecourse and New Road cricket ground.
sights: Cathedral above the Severn, where King John is buried.
Civil War museum in a historic building.
eat: Created in Worcester by Lea & Perrins.
night: Music and comedy in a historic chapel.
arrive: Worcester Foregate Street and Shrub Hill stations have trains to Birmingham and London Paddington. Birmingham Airport is about 45 minutes away.
around: Walkable centre; First buses.
pass: First day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for the river and cricket.
tip: Walk the riverside path to see the cathedral from the opposite bank.

intro: A hilltop city crowned by a vast Gothic cathedral and a castle holding a Magna Carta.
areas: Independent shops on one of England’s steepest streets.
sights: Once the world’s tallest building, still a Gothic masterpiece.
Walk the walls; home to a 1215 Magna Carta.
Historic street linking downhill and uphill.
eat: Cafés and tearooms near the cathedral.
arrive: Lincoln station has trains to London King’s Cross (some direct) and Nottingham. East Midlands and Humberside airports are about an hour away.
around: Walk, but be ready for Steep Hill; Stagecoach buses cover the city.
pass: Stagecoach day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn; the Christmas market (early December).
tip: Wear good shoes: Steep Hill lives up to its name.

intro: A walled medieval city of Viking history, a mighty minster and the timber-framed Shambles.
areas: The Minster, the Shambles and Stonegate.
Historic street of bars and restaurants.
The Ouse, the Abbey ruins and the Yorkshire Museum.
sights: One of Europe’s largest Gothic cathedrals.
The longest medieval town walls in England.
Viking York recreated on its excavation site.
eat: Bettys tearooms is a famous stop.
night: Many inns claim to be the city’s most haunted.
arrive: York station has fast trains to London King’s Cross (about two hours), Edinburgh and Manchester. Leeds Bradford Airport is about an hour away.
around: Walk; the centre is compact. First and Park & Ride buses for the outskirts.
pass: Park & Ride and bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn; the Christmas markets; the Viking Festival in February.
tip: Walk the walls early in the morning before the crowds.

intro: A maritime city on the Humber with a revived old town, a spectacular aquarium and free museums.
areas: Cobbled streets, museums and historic pubs.
Creative quarter with bars and galleries.
sights: One of the world’s longest single-span suspension bridges.
eat: A local favourite from chip shops.
arrive: Hull Paragon station has trains to London King’s Cross and Leeds. Ferries sail to Rotterdam. Humberside Airport is about 40 minutes away.
around: Walkable centre; Stagecoach and East Yorkshire buses.
pass: Bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn.
tip: Walk the Fish Trail, a set of pavement sculptures across the Old Town.

intro: UK City of Culture 2025, with a famous curry scene, a photography museum and the moors close by.
areas: City Hall and the mirror pool.
World Heritage model village on the city’s edge.
sights: Model village and gallery with David Hockney works.
eat: Bradford’s South Asian restaurants are famous.
night: Concerts and shows in the restored Odeon.
arrive: Leeds Bradford Airport is about 20–30 minutes away. Bradford Interchange and Forster Square stations link to Leeds and Manchester.
around: First buses and local trains; Saltaire is a short train ride.
pass: West Yorkshire MCard day tickets; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for the moors.
tip: Take the train to Saltaire, then walk the canal towpath.

intro: A historic market town and racing capital, with the oldest classic horse race and a busy rail hub.
areas: Town Moor, home of the St Leger.
sights: Home of the St Leger, the oldest of the five British classics.
Victorian church by George Gilbert Scott.
eat: Historic market with a fish market and food hall.
night: Summer music nights at the racecourse.
arrive: Doncaster station is on the East Coast Main Line, about 1h40 from London King’s Cross.
around: First buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: Travel South Yorkshire day tickets; check current fares.
when: September for the St Leger Festival.
tip: Book hotels early for the St Leger Festival in September.

intro: A Teesside town of steel heritage, a giant transporter bridge and modern art, between the moors and the coast.
areas: Centre Square and the Town Hall.
The Transporter Bridge and the Tees.
sights: Rare working transporter bridge (check operating status).
eat: On the coast, an hour away.
arrive: Middlesbrough station has trains to Newcastle, York and Whitby (via the Esk Valley line). Teesside International Airport is about 20 minutes away.
around: Arriva and Stagecoach buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: Bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for the moors and coast.
tip: Try a parmo, then walk it off on Roseberry Topping.

intro: A seaside city on the Wear with sandy beaches, a glass centre and the Stadium of Light.
areas: Keel Square, Sunniside and the Empire.
National Glass Centre and Stadium of Light.
sights: Victorian pier with seasonal lighthouse tours.
Free museum with a tropical glasshouse.
arrive: Newcastle International Airport is about 30 minutes away. The Tyne and Wear Metro and Sunderland station link to Newcastle.
around: Tyne and Wear Metro and Go North East / Stagecoach buses.
pass: Metro day tickets and Pop cards; check current fares.
when: Summer for the beaches and the Sunderland Airshow (check dates).
tip: Walk from Roker to Seaburn along the seafront.

intro: A historic border city with a red sandstone castle, a cathedral and Hadrian’s Wall on its doorstep.
sights: Medieval castle on the Scottish border.
arrive: Carlisle station has trains to London Euston, Glasgow, Newcastle and the Settle–Carlisle line. Newcastle and Glasgow airports are about 90 minutes away.
around: Walkable centre; Stagecoach buses to the Lakes and Hadrian’s Wall.
pass: Stagecoach day tickets; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for Hadrian’s Wall walks.
tip: Ride the scenic Settle–Carlisle railway.
